description: Read one parameter off the parametric object attached to each incoming space, node or segment and publish it as a matrix a Math Engine can use. The counterpart of Set Object Param.
instructions:
Filter by Type answers WHICH spaces; this answers WHAT THEY SAY. Wire a Spaces bundle in and it reads the named parameter off each space's attached object.

`val-values` is an N x 2 matrix of `[indexInTheIncomingBundle, value]`, and the index is what makes it usable: a Math Engine looping over the same bundle can look a space's value up by position, and a row is present only for spaces that actually carry the parameter. `val-count` is how many were found, `val-missing` how many were not — a missing count equal to the bundle size means the parameter name is wrong or nothing is attached.

VALUES ARE NUMERIC. A matrix holds numbers, so a parameter that does not parse as one is reported in `missing` rather than silently written as 0 — a plot with no Number is genuinely unknown, not plot zero. Read a numeric parameter here (Number, Thickness, a checkbox as 1/0); a select or a free-text parameter is not something an expression can carry.

The geometry passes straight through, so this can sit mid-chain without disturbing the pipeline.

IDENTITY IS RESOLVED BY POSITION IN THE CANVAS BUNDLE — the same rule Filter by Type and Set Object Param follow — so keep it on a path that has not rebuilt the geometry.

SPACES, NODES AND SEGMENTS. All three carry parametric objects, so all three can be addressed; `Host` picks which, and Auto is right whenever the bundle came straight off the Canvas node. Identity is resolved by POSITION IN THAT COLLECTION, so keep this on a path that has not rebuilt the geometry - and note that index 3 means a different element in each of the three, which is why the choice is explicit rather than inferred from the parameter name.

parameters.label: Host
parameters.help: Which canvas collection the incoming bundle addresses. Auto matches the bundle against the canvas's own arrays by reference and falls back to its shape (1 point = node, 2 = segment, 3+ = space).
